newsitem.title: USA: Perdigao sets pasta, vegetable marketing.
newsitem.headline: Perdigao sets pasta, vegetable marketing.

text.p: Perdigao SA Comercio e Industria will begin distributing fresh pasta and frozen vegetables next month, Chief Financial Officer Wang Wei Chang told security analysts.

"We are a distribution company with a strong network of warehouses and trucks" now distributing the company's refrigerated and frozen meat products, he explained in a presentation Thursday, the last in a series of analysts' presentations in the U.S. the past three weeks.
The pasta will be produced by an Argentine company that will handle advertising in Brazil while Perdigao distributes the product for a contracted margin, Chang said.
At the same time, he said, the Argentine company will distribute Perdigao meat products in Argentina, where Perdigao will be responsible for advertising.
He said the company is "not looking for much profit" on the frozen vegetables it will be importing from Belgium. Rather, Perdigao plans to establish a brand name.
"Our plan is to use the brand name for other products," Change said.
"We see ourselves more as a distribution company" than a meat packer, Chief Executive Officer Nildemar Secches said.
Perdigao's "network is an asset," he said, adding logistics are "very important to us."

Chang said the company has completed 85 percent of the optimization begun in 1994. When it is complete next year, the company's production of poultry meat will have increased 57.4 percent to 255,000 tons per year and pork 54.1 percent to 245,000 tons per year.
Spending on this project is expected to drop to U.S. $74 million this year from $127 million in 1996, he said.
Chang said another $20 million will be spent this year ast the first investment on the company's new expansion program.
In 1998 through 2003, Perdigao expects to spend $286 million on the new expansion program, brining 1994 to 2003 outlays to 570 million.

In 1999, he continued, the first parts of the new expansion will be put into operation. And by 2003, the company expects another 54.9 percent net increase in poultry meat production and 61.2 percent net increase in port production, with both expected to total 395,000 tons per year in 2003.

He said the company has a long term contract to buy eggs from Tyson Foods Inc to improve the quality of chicks Perdigao distributes to farmers that grow them to mature chickens under contract to the company.
Behind the company's expansion, Chang said, is its belief that the Brazilian poultry and pork market, which now totals $22 billion a year, is growing seven percent per year.
Perdigao also expects to continue to export at least 20 percent of its production each year, Seeches said.
